responseText: {"title":"Face as Frequency","question":"When a face is built from competing marks, colors, and symbols, what—if anything—does it still communicate?","introduction":"Every work here is, technically, a face. But each one is also a collision: of color temperatures, mark systems, eye shapes, tooth rows, and grounds that refuse to stay back. This exhibition moves from faces that hold their form through a single dominant feature, into heads where every element broadcasts at once, and finally to figures where the face begins to dissolve into its own noise.","closing":"Twenty-six faces, each assembled from marks that pull in different directions. Whether anything coherent survives that competition is a question each work leaves open.","chapters":[{"title":"One Thing in Charge","introduction":"These faces organize themselves around a single dominant element—an oversized head, a sealed gaze, a split down the middle—that holds the composition together even as smaller marks scatter around it.","stops":[{"slot":"W003","whyHere":"The vast golden head crowds out everything else; lavender lenses and scattered triangles orbit it without challenging its dominance.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W008","whyHere":"A clean vertical split divides warm from dark, replacing W003's radiant mass with a face that is literally two competing halves.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where W003 is unified by warm yellow volume, W008 fractures along a single color boundary, making division the organizing principle."},{"slot":"W015","whyHere":"Rectangular glasses seal the eyes entirely; the single vivid lip becomes the only open channel in an otherwise blocked face.","transitionFromPrevious":"W008's split is chromatic; W015's blockage is architectural—dark frames physically close off the upper face, redirecting attention downward."},{"slot":"W065","whyHere":"Wide blue sunglasses with mirrored yellow reflections seal the eyes again, but here the sealed face floats against unbroken red, ornament piled onto opacity.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both W015 and W065 use opaque eyewear to withhold expression; W065 adds scribbled hair and scattered dots that make the concealment feel festive rather than guarded."}]},{"title":"The Mouth Takes Over","introduction":"Here the mouth—teeth, jaw, open gap—moves from supporting feature to compositional engine, pulling the eye downward and forward with blunt force.","stops":[{"slot":"W033","whyHere":"A rigid white tooth grid and tilted sunglasses split the face into sealed top and shouting bottom, with warm rays fanning behind.","transitionFromPrevious":"W065's sealed eyes reappear here, but now a wide tooth grid below them shifts the balance from concealment toward confrontation."},{"slot":"W050","whyHere":"A wide-open mouth with a dark central gap dominates the lower half; scattered hearts above read as frantic rather than tender against the teal ground.","transitionFromPrevious":"W033's teeth are bared but contained; W050's mouth opens into a dark cavity, adding urgency to what was already a shout."},{"slot":"W021","whyHere":"Heavy black skull-mass with red-hatched eye sockets and bared white teeth, softened by loose pink and purple loops that drift past the jaw.","transitionFromPrevious":"W050's mouth commands a bright, busy surface; W021 buries its teeth in a dark form, making the grin feel heavier and more ambiguous."},{"slot":"W036","whyHere":"Two tooth-bearing forms share the frame—a large pale row and a smaller sharp-toothed head—with magenta rings drawing unequal attention to each.","transitionFromPrevious":"W021 has one face with one mouth; W036 doubles the tooth motif across two unequal heads, turning the jaw into a repeated, almost absurd refrain."},{"slot":"W005","whyHere":"Dense black lines pool at the base around a downturned mouth; the figure reads as cornered, its small white teeth part of a larger tangle of pressure.","transitionFromPrevious":"W036's two mouths feel confrontational; W005 compresses the same energy into a single crouched figure, the teeth almost buried under the weight of surrounding marks."}]},{"title":"Eyes That Broadcast","introduction":"These works shift emphasis upward: eyes become targets, spirals, mismatched lenses, or single overwhelming orbs—each a different kind of signal competing with the face around it.","stops":[{"slot":"W007","whyHere":"A single red-iris eye dominates like a wound; teal bars and a crosshatched grid below it read as a cage sealing the lower face.","transitionFromPrevious":"W005's eyes stare outward from a dense tangle; W007 isolates one eye as the entire subject, surrounding it with containment structures."},{"slot":"W028","whyHere":"One oversized eye ringed by tooth-like zigzags and pink spikes stares from a swirling maroon cavity; a small clover and lips at the lower left offer a quiet counterpoint.","transitionFromPrevious":"W007's eye is framed by geometric bars; W028's eye is framed by organic spikes and dripping marks, making the stare feel more visceral and less architectural."},{"slot":"W052","whyHere":"Two spiral clusters of different hues form asymmetric eye-like zones; a toothy bar anchors the lower half while white scribbles blur every boundary.","transitionFromPrevious":"W028 has one dominant eye; W052 distributes the eye-function across two competing spirals, so the gaze becomes plural and off-balance."},{"slot":"W009","whyHere":"Mismatched eyes topped by green hearts stare from a dense field of cyan arcs and yellow bands; the broad toothy mouth refuses to let the eyes hold focus alone.","transitionFromPrevious":"W052's spirals are the whole face; W009 restores a full face but packs every element—eyes, mouth, background—at equal volume, so nothing can dominate."},{"slot":"W023","whyHere":"Target-like concentric eyes are the most controlled marks in an otherwise restless surface of scribble tangles and flat dark planes, lending the figure a watchful stillness.","transitionFromPrevious":"W009's eyes compete with everything around them; W023's eyes are the calmest element, creating tension by contrast with the frantic marks surrounding them."},{"slot":"W056","whyHere":"Two unequal eyes—a dark outlined oval and a gold-ringed stare—pull attention across a tilted face; heavy outlines hold the form while thinner lines wander past its edges.","transitionFromPrevious":"W023's eyes are symmetrically concentric; W056's eyes are visibly unequal in shape and color, making the asymmetry itself the subject."}]},{"title":"Faces Under Pressure","introduction":"These works pack the face—or the space around it—so densely with competing marks, symbols, and color zones that the face itself begins to feel like one element among many rather than the organizing center.","stops":[{"slot":"W037","whyHere":"A rounded outline crammed with crown, spoked wheel, dotted borders, and a red zigzag jaw reads as a face and a packed machine simultaneously.","transitionFromPrevious":"W056's face is held together by heavy outlines; W037's outline contains so much competing content that the face-reading becomes unstable."},{"slot":"W011","whyHere":"Four overlapping head-forms crowd the frame, each in a different color zone, stitched together by a repeated tooth motif that runs across all of them.","transitionFromPrevious":"W037 packs one face-container past capacity; W011 multiplies the containers, so the question of which face to read becomes unanswerable."},{"slot":"W019","whyHere":"A head locked in scaffolding of heavy black and red framing lines, with gray block-letter shapes crowding the yellow ground like half-erased graffiti.","transitionFromPrevious":"W011's faces compete with each other; W019's single face competes with text-like shapes in its ground, blurring the boundary between figure and annotation."},{"slot":"W026","whyHere":"Against saturated red, overlapping loops of black, sky blue, and white compete for space; small hearts and a lavender spot at the base are easy to miss beneath the commotion.","transitionFromPrevious":"W019's ground presses in with letter-shapes; W026's ground and figure merge into a single knotted density, making the face almost impossible to locate."},{"slot":"W049","whyHere":"The figure emerges from total black as a tangle of color and wire-like line; red-rimmed eyes hold a stillness that contrasts sharply with the surrounding chaos.","transitionFromPrevious":"W026 dissolves into its red ground; W049 dissolves into black, but two red-rimmed eyes hold their position, offering the only stable point in the composition."}]},{"title":"Signal and Residue","introduction":"The final group: faces that have absorbed their own noise and arrived somewhere quieter—not resolved, but settled into a particular register of mark, color, and posture.","stops":[{"slot":"W022","whyHere":"Pale rays push outward from behind the head; warm tones pool on one side, cool on the other, splitting the face into contrasting temperatures without breaking its outline.","transitionFromPrevious":"W049 emerges from darkness; W022 radiates outward into light, reversing the direction of pressure while keeping the face's expression mid-shift."},{"slot":"W024","whyHere":"Fanning rays push outward from the jaw as if heat or sound is escaping; thick color patches build mass while thin neon scribbles hover above like static.","transitionFromPrevious":"W022's rays emanate from behind the head; W024's rays push from the jaw itself, making the radiation feel like something the face is producing rather than receiving."},{"slot":"W040","whyHere":"Every surface carries a different fill—scribble, rainbow bands, hatching—locked into compartments by heavy black outlines, giving the head a stained-glass quality.","transitionFromPrevious":"W024's marks feel like escaping energy; W040's marks are contained within rigid outlines, turning the same density into something more structured and sealed."},{"slot":"W045","whyHere":"A polka-dot field pushes the figure forward like a cut-out; oversized sunglasses hide expression, leaving the cigarette and cap tilt to carry the attitude.","transitionFromPrevious":"W040's face is packed with competing fills; W045 simplifies to a flat patterned ground and a single withheld expression, making restraint feel like its own kind of noise."},{"slot":"W046","whyHere":"Flat blue ground, tangled scribble lines holding soft color patches together, open mouth and mismatched eyes caught mid-shout—a face assembled from interference.","transitionFromPrevious":"W045 withholds expression behind sunglasses; W046 opens the mouth wide, but the surrounding scribble and flat ground make the shout feel suspended rather than released."},{"slot":"W063","whyHere":"A profile tilting into the frame, built from overlapping color patches that never solidify; a single red line cuts across the face, and vertical stripes drape from the jaw like an afterimage.","transitionFromPrevious":"W046 faces forward with a frozen shout; W063 turns away in profile, its marks dissolving into the purple ground, leaving expression as a residue rather than a statement."}]}]}
